query: How can we statistically justify a 30‑episode pilot given expected per‑label instance counts and class imbalance, and what explicit stop/grow criteria should determine scaling to 60–100 episodes?

response.query: How can we statistically justify a 30‑episode pilot given expected per‑label instance counts and class imbalance, and what explicit stop/grow criteria should determine scaling to 60–100 episodes?
response.answer: To justify a 30-episode pilot, analyze per-label instance counts and class imbalance; scale to 60–100 episodes based on model performance metrics and data diversity. Use accuracy, precision, and recall as stop/grow criteria.

results.title: News
results.content: Some highlights include talks from our 2025 Portal Documentation recipients including The Circus, with St Mary’s Special School with Vocalist Deirdre Shannon, Art Teacher Ina Olohan and Teacher Siobhán Doughty; a creative workshop: XR Drawing & Sculpting for Creative Practice, Education and Youth Engagement, with Creative Technologist Barry “Hawkie” Haughey; and a presentation and discussion: From Harmonic to Chorus: Amplifying Student Voice through Creative STEAM Engagement, with Dr. Sharon Shannon and Writer – Researcher Adam Breen. The aim and structure of the VTS: Neighbourhood Schools project is to continue using Visual Thinking Strategies to add to the knowledge of the arts and build on the sense of place and experience that the children on Central Model N.S have and to share that experience with their neighbours through working in close collaboration with two schools (St. Mary’s N.S, Fairview and St. Vincent’s B.N.S, Ballybough) with trained VTS practitioners in each of the schools.

results.title: Eye Matter Matters/Newsletter
results.content: This is a fortnightly publication where Eye Matter shares news and information about events and activities, members’ experiences and other items of interest. Eye Matter’s member and RNIB’s volunteer, Charmaine who took part in this event said, “I was delighted to be part of this presentation about the importance of ensuring early access to rehabilitation. Eye Matter was delighted to welcome many new members and volunteers as the charity continued to grow and reach more visually impaired people. In the past 12 months, Eye Matter members have been invited to join over 200 free Zoom events and 36 in person outings. Eye Matter’s twice weekly “fun and friendly social hours” continued to bring members together to laugh and chat in an informal and relaxed Zoom room whilst monthly “Bounce” meetings have been another space for members to share problems and find solutions or workarounds for a visually impaired life.
